Subject: Acme.ai — Post-call recap: integration & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Customer support search is slow and often returns low-relevance results for intent-based queries.
- Need structured outputs for routing to the right internal team (billing, technical, legal) to avoid manual tagging.
- Real-time chat UI requires sub-500ms latencies for conversational responses to feel native.
- Desire to re-rank retrieval candidates server-side (embeddings -> rerank) to improve precision.

What we discussed as the integration approach:
- Use Redwood SDK for realtime streaming responses to the web UI (function-calling + streaming tokens).
- Use structured output schema (function calling or structured JSON) for ticket classification and routing.
- Embeddings pipeline: batch embeddings for nightly index updates + on-demand mini-batches for new docs; reranking layer before final scoring.
- Start with a canary using redwood-llm-v2-small for low-latency routing, then expand to the v2 model for quality-sensitive flows.

Timeline & next steps:
1) Marissa to share a 1-page integration plan and proposed SOW (attached: integration_plan.pdf).
2) Devon/Julia to share security questionnaire and procurement timeline.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineering team + our solutions engineer (suggested: Wed, Jun 30, 10:00 AM PT).
4) Nikhil to follow up on pricing/commit options after we confirm expected qps and latency SLOs.

Proposed owners:
- Redwood: Marissa (sales) / Connor (solutions engineering) / Nikhil (pricing)
- Acme: Devon (product) / Julia (engineering) / Procurement (procurement@acme.ai)

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Approx qps/concurrent users for the chat (you mentioned 600 daily active agents — can you confirm concurrent peaks?).
- Are there hard PII/e2e encryption requirements for the embeddings index?
- Any must-have on retention or audit logs (SOC2 scope)?

I'll tentatively book Wed 10am PT for the tech deep-dive; if that doesn't work, please suggest alternatives.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,

Great — quick answers and more detail below.

Security questionnaire: Connor (cc'd below in later message) will own technical answers. Estimated turnaround for the completed questionnaire: 3 business days once we have any required infra notes from you (PII/encryption retention details).

Latency & model guidance:
- Canary path: redwood-llm-v2-small -> expected generation p50 ~120–200ms for short responses (under 128 tokens) on dedicated instances with batching tuned, p95 ~350–500ms depending on context length.
- With reranking step (embeddings retrieval + light neural rerank), expect added ~80–150ms in the common case; so end-to-end p50 ~200–350ms is reasonable for short/typical queries.
- For high-quality responses (long-form or multi-step reasoning) use redwood-llm-v2 — expect higher latency but better accuracy; we can route these requests to a different pool.

Integration notes (practical):
- Streaming + function-calling: we recommend enabling token streaming and function-calling concurrently. Use streaming to render partial results in the UI, but emit a final structured payload (function call result or structured JSON) for routing/ticket creation.
- SDK change: we'll share a small SDK patch that adds a structured-output helper which validates function-call schemas client-side and patches the websocket streaming API to emit chunked JSON frames. This is non-breaking for most integrations.
- Embeddings & reranking: run nightly bulk embeddings for the corpus + a lightweight online mini-batch for newly created docs. Reranker should run on top of the top-K retrieval (K=10) before final scoring.

Next steps:
- I'll upload the detailed one-pager and our sample integration sketch (integration_design_sketch.png) to the Drive link and share a GitHub sample repo.
- Connor, are you able to take the technical deep-dive Wed 10am PT? If yes, please include a short agenda focused on SDK auth, streaming schema, and embeddings pipeline.

Thanks — I'm attaching an example pseudocode snippet for streaming+function call below (for reference):

// pseudocode
const stream = redwood.sdk.stream({model: 'redwood-llm-v2-small'});
stream.on('chunk', (c) => renderPartial(c.text));
stream.on('function_call', (fn) => {
  const parsed = JSON.parse(fn.payload);
  // validate against ticket schema then send to routing service
});

Best,
Marissa
